summary: Packet ws08-ws09-declared-attachment-modes is implemented. Without -D warnings, clippy finishes. It prints many pedantic warnings across model-gateway, including sse.rs:4782 and :7657 (redundant field names) and tool_loop.rs:7743 (similar binding names). I did not check which of these are new.

residual_risks: The packet's clippy gate (`cargo clippy -p model-gateway --lib --tests -- -D warnings`) cannot pass. It stops on lints already present in crates/mp-content-safety (normalize.rs:60, scan.rs:165) and on about 500 pedantic findings that already exist in model-gateway. So none of the new lines has been checked under -D warnings in a gated run. The coder says the 6 findings their draft added were fixed.

The answer-request wiring (sse.rs:3168-3189) and the history-shed re-check (sse.rs:3487-3491) have no unit test, because sse.rs has no harness for them. They are covered only by compiling and by review. Reviewed: between render and the answer, `messages` is reassigned only by the research, forced-search and tool-round results, and the shed recomputes the plan through plan_for. So a stale plan cannot be sent.

A plan exists only when CacheOptions selects PromptOrder::StablePrefix. Routes that CacheOptions::for_route forces to Legacy (and any turn with the stable-order switch off) still send no tiers. This matches the brief, but the reach of D1-445/446 is limited to the stable-prefix routes. The coder's deploy note on this point is cut off in the report.

The ZDR gate is `!effective_zdr` only. It does not also check `retention_class.is_some()`, which matches the existing cache_prefix gate at sse.rs:3203. If an ephemeral retention class should also suppress provider prompt caching, both gates would need to change together. That is out of scope here.
plan_for compares only role and content (as the brief specifies). A ChatMessage whose other fields change while role and content stay the same would still match.
Two new lines exceed rustfmt width: the `.all(...)` closure in prompt_context.rs plan_for and the `decision_tiers` binding in tool_loop.rs. This is cosmetic. tool_loop.rs already has many long lines.

Line endings: the working copies of prompt_context.rs and tool_loop.rs are CRLF and sse.rs is LF, while the HEAD blobs are LF with core.autocrlf=true. The diff is content-only (463+/8-), so no whole-file churn was added.
deploy_notes: No proto, env-var or compose change, and both switches stay as they are. With the stable order off, or on a ZDR turn, requests are unchanged: no plan and the same messages. Coverage gap for the lead to decide: the plan exists only when CacheOptions is StablePrefix, and CacheOptions::for_route (prompt_context.rs) forces Legacy on Claude and unhinted turns. So an Anthropic inline turn still sends no plan. The plan reaches the wire only on OpenAI-pinned turns with the stable switch on, and only the Anthropic provider reads it (inference-core provider/anthropic.rs:250-300), so on those turns it has no effect unless inference-core fails over to Anthropic. Making Claude inline turns use the tiered order would change their prompt order, so that needs an owner decision before this packet can be counted as delivering WS02-S9 to inline chat. Other packets are editing the same worktree (attachment_policy.rs, http_routes.rs, model_access.rs, attachment_policy_contract.rs, inference-core grpc.rs); my runs compiled against those in-progress edits. The computed task text listed no editable files, but the packet record names the three files above, which are the only ones I changed. No database-backed tests were written.
summary: Carried the composer's stable-order prompt-tier plan into the inline chat tool rounds and the answer call (D1-445, D1-446). prompt_context.rs gains render_planned (Legacy: the same render output and no plan; StablePrefix: the tiered render plus its plan), wire_plan (the counts as the proto PromptTierPlan, None when both are zero) and plan_for, which returns the plan only while the first stable+context messages of the outgoing list equal the composed ones (role and content) and are all system. sse.rs takes the plan at render, drops it on ZDR turns, and passes it only where plan_for confirms the head: to the tool rounds (re-checked after the research and forced-search passes), to the answer request, and after a history shed. tool_loop.rs takes a trailing prompt_tiers parameter on run_tool_rounds_for_model and run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments (run_tool_rounds passes None), snapshots the composed head at entry, and sets the decision InferRequest's prompt_tiers through plan_for. Legacy-order and switch-off requests are unchanged; the proto is unchanged. Deviations: no inference double existed in tool_loop tests, so I wrote a RecordingCore (all 21 InferenceCore RPCs, only Infer records) to test the decision wiring; the shed rule keeps the plan whenever the head survives rather than sending None on any rewrite; sse.rs calls render_planned, which uses the same stable render path as render_tiered (render_tiered is unchanged). The answer-request and shed wiring have no unit test because sse.rs has no harness for it; they are covered by compile, review and the contract tests.
